coaching.summary: The graph captures the core tension between enterprise revenue protection and bottom-up growth, but it underweights how each option differentially affects the top-10 accounts and lacks a mechanism linking enterprise concentration directly to NRR. Sharpening those links and adding a usage-floor constraint will make the trade-offs between the three live options much clearer.

strengthen_items.label: Wire enterprise concentration directly to NRR
strengthen_items.detail: Top-10 Account Revenue Concentration currently only flows to Enterprise Account Downsell or Churn, but 40% revenue concentration means even modest downsell directly moves Net Revenue Retention—add an edge from Top-10 Account Revenue Concentration to Net Revenue Retention to make that arithmetic visible.

strengthen_items.label: Quantify the revenue exposure per option for top-10 accounts
strengthen_items.detail: Assign a numeric range to Enterprise Account Revenue Exposure under each option (e.g., estimated ARR at risk if top-10 reprice to actual usage) so Hybrid Platform Fee Plus Usage and Usage Pricing for New Logos Only can be compared against the 110% NRR threshold rather than ranked qualitatively.

strengthen_items.label: Add a minimum-commit or usage-floor constraint
strengthen_items.detail: A contractual usage floor on enterprise accounts is the primary lever that lets Hybrid Platform Fee Plus Usage protect NRR while still enabling bottom-up adoption; modeling it as an explicit constraint node would show which options can satisfy it and which cannot.

strengthen_items.label: Separate NRR and bottom-up adoption into two ranked goals
strengthen_items.detail: Achieve Net Revenue Retention Above 110% While Enabling Bottom-Up Adoption bundles two potentially conflicting success criteria—clarify whether 110% NRR is a hard constraint or a target, and whether bottom-up adoption is a leading indicator or a co-equal goal, so trade-off decisions have a clear tiebreaker.

elements_considered_but_excluded: Competitive pricing pressure node — relevant but not mentioned in brief and would require new factor
Customer success capacity node — operational but outside graph scope
Grandfathering / price-lock option — brief implies three live options are exhaustive

bias_signals.detail: The brief assumes usage-based pricing will improve new logo conversion without evidence of Market Appetite for Usage-Based Pricing strength in the actual segment; this assumption flows unchecked into New Logo Revenue Growth.

Framing Keep Per-Seat Pricing (Status Quo) as a live option alongside three transition strategies may anchor deliberation toward inaction; the status quo's own NRR trajectory under seat-pricing pressure is not modeled.

Concentration on the top-10 accounts' downside risk may cause the team to underweight the compounding upside of Bottom-Up Usage Adoption Enablement on New Logo Revenue Growth over a multi-year horizon.
